skill.name: quality-fixer
skill.description: Apply Python quality fixes with formatter, linter, and verification workflows for Black, isort, Ruff, and Make-based checks.
skill.summary: Fix Python formatting and lint issues while guiding review and verification.
skill.author: Atyantik

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks around examples and prose, not Ruby shell execution. A smaller set is confirmed because the skill recommends Git operations that can discard local work or publish changes if followed automatically.

remediation.suggestion: Replace hard reset and checkout rollback commands with non-destructive review steps, or require explicit user confirmation before any revert.

remediation.issue: Commit and push commands in quality workflows
remediation.suggestion: Remove automated commit and push steps from the skill. Tell users to review diffs and run source-control commands manually.

remediation.issue: Project-defined quality commands can execute local scripts
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before running Make or uv commands in unfamiliar repositories. Prefer dry-run checks before applying fixes.

content.value_statement: Python projects often fail format, lint, or quality gates near commit time. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through formatter, Ruff, and verification workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Black and isort formatting for Python source and tests.
Applies Ruff auto-fixes for safe lint issues such as unused imports.
Explains how to resolve Black and Ruff formatter conflicts.
Supports dry-run review before applying larger quality changes.
Provides a structured report of modified files, fixes, and check results.
limitations: Does not fix business logic, algorithms, or design problems.
Does not write missing tests or repair failing tests.
Assumes the project already uses Python quality tools such as Black, isort, Ruff, and Make.
Git commands in examples should require user review before execution.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Before Commit
use_cases.description: Format code, sort imports, apply safe lint fixes, and verify the result before a developer creates a commit.

use_cases.title: Resolve CI Quality Failures
use_cases.description: Use local formatter and lint workflows to address quality failures reported by a continuous integration job.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Formatting
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Black, isort, and Ruff practices across source files and tests during routine maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Current Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality-fixer skill to format my Python changes, apply safe lint fixes, and show me the files changed.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Before Applying
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-fixer in preview mode for src and tests. Show likely formatter and Ruff changes before applying them.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Tool Conflicts
prompt_templates.scenario: Black and Ruff disagree on formatting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-fixer to identify Black and Ruff conflicts, resolve long-line issues, and verify both tools pass.

prompt_templates.title: Recover CI Quality Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow after a failed build.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-fixer to inspect the CI quality failure, apply only safe fixes, run verification, and summarize remaining manual work.

output_examples.input: A feature branch has import ordering and Ruff errors after several Python files changed.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports that imports were sorted, unused imports were removed, formatting was applied, and verification still needs user review.

output_examples.input: Black passes, but Ruff reports long-line conflicts in error messages.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains which messages were split or extracted, then summarizes the files that need a final diff review.

output_examples.input: A CI quality job failed after a merge from main.
output_examples.output: The assistant separates safe formatting fixes from manual issues, runs local verification, and lists any unresolved checks.

best_practices: Start with preview or dry-run checks when working in an unfamiliar repository.
Review the diff before accepting formatter, lint, or import changes.
Run tests after applying quality fixes because formatting can reveal hidden issues.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-commit or push changes without explicit user approval.
Do not use destructive Git rollback commands as the first recovery step.
Do not apply auto-fixes to generated code unless the project allows it.

faq.question: What tools does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Python projects that use Black, isort, Ruff, Make targets, and related quality checks.

faq.question: Can it fix failing tests?
faq.answer: No. It can run or recommend verification, but test failures require separate debugging.

faq.question: Does it change code behavior?
faq.answer: It is intended for safe formatting and lint fixes, but every diff still needs review.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Should it run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Git commit, push, reset, and checkout operations should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: When should I use preview mode?
faq.answer: Use preview mode before large cleanup work or when the repository configuration is unfamiliar.
